data.title: Mupirocin 2% cream/ointment
data.summary: II Antibacterials · Monoxycarbolic acid antibiotic (pseudomonic acid A, from Pseudomonas fluorescens)
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Monoxycarbolic acid antibiotic (pseudomonic acid A, from Pseudomonas fluorescens)

## Mechanism of action
- Reversibly binds bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase → stops protein synthesis
- Unique target — no cross-resistance with other antibiotics
- Bacteriostatic at low concentration, bactericidal at the high concentrations reached on skin
- Active against Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA) and Streptococcus pyogenes

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Impetigo (localised), secondarily infected eczema, folliculitis, small infected wounds
- Nasal decolonisation of S. aureus/MRSA carriers (recurrent furunculosis, before surgery)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply 2–3 times daily for 5–10 days
- Nasal ointment: twice daily into both nostrils for 5 days (with chlorhexidine body washes for recurrent boils)

## Adverse effects
- Burning, itching
- Polyethylene glycol (ointment base) can be absorbed from large wounds → nephrotoxicity (avoid in renal impairment on extensive raw areas)
- Resistance with prolonged or repeated use (low-level and high-level mupA-mediated)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; large burns or open wounds in renal impairment (PEG base)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Target: isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase
- Nasal decolonisation for recurrent furunculosis
- Limit course to under 10 days to prevent resistance

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41; Khopkar ch.18. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
